title: Teaching Johnny Lindsay to read a hard cornet piece
summary: He tells of giving trombonist Johnny Lindsay lessons and testing him on a difficult piece, using shanks on the cornet; Lindsay later died in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: The division. If you know the lives, you can't play. Some of them know the music though. They get up there, they play, they play, but when you come to a club, you play with somebody else you don't know why you're at. It's just as bad. Well I tried to show them. Johnny Lindsay, he was playing with the rubber shows. He's in the, Johnny Lindsay plays trombone. And he was playing at the larynx thing. And I was living right there at that chord. See that chord you've got there, five or twelve dolphins. Oh yeah, yeah. Johnny Lindsay, when they play at night, then they get off for lunch, you know, and go back to play for that matinee in the evening. He'd come and he took two, three lessons. Yeah. And so first night I brought him in the final room, then I had a little music and we played together. He played. But he wasn't sure. He could play to me but he wasn't sure. So he played and I had a piece of music from Liofice. It was the walls. And I think it was in three flats. And we used using that long shank. Is that what?
You see they had two shanks there. Put it in the key of A or something. Put the key in there, change key.

On the cornet. Oh, I see. You used to have a long shank that puts you in A and then you take that off, put the other shank on and puts you in B. Oh, I see, yeah. You see? And I took that shank off and I put it in A and I said if you could play this, I said you can go to myself. And so I started a brand new piece. I just come from Liofice. I had two pieces coming. I said this is tough old. It's about five shops I think it was. Five flats for him and shops for me. I said let's play this again.

He died about eight years ago.
He died. In Chicago. Yes, and I haven't saw him since. He went up to stay in Chicago. He took three lessons with me. And I told him he could go, but he could play. He knows it. But he wasn't sure.
